A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DecAlign framework, with matching core equations and benchmark experiments. All supplied pages are readable. Although v1 refers to an appendix that is not included, v2 supplies Appendices A–C; their contents can be assessed as newly available documentation without assuming changes to previously undocumented procedures.

before.justification: v1 reports original DecAlign benchmark results, component ablations, confusion matrices, modality-gap visualizations and parameter sensitivity experiments in Tables 1–4 and Figures 4–7.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and ablation results and reports additional comparison metrics and visualization evidence in the main text and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The core equations and architecture are retained; PDE and separate transformers already appear in v1 Figure 3. However, Section 3.1 changes from preserving temporal length to transforming modalities to a common length Ts, while both versions already denote outputs using Ts. The PDFs do not resolve whether this is a procedural change or a correction to the description.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate audiovisual and textual sentiment/emotion prediction on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, CH-SIMS and six-class IEMOCAP. The additional CH-SIMS metrics retain existing coverage: positive, neutral and negative categories already appear in v1 Figure 5.

E2.justification: ReconBoost replaces MCIS in the MOSI, MOSEI and IEMOCAP comparison tables. For CH-SIMS, v2 introduces ReconBoost in Table 1 while retaining MCIS in Appendix Table 7. The other comparator identities remain unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 Table 7 adds Acc-3 and Corr to the CH-SIMS evaluation, beyond v1's tabulated MAE and F1. Other benchmark metrics are retained. The newly stated splits, training epochs and batch size disclose existing experimental settings without establishing that those settings changed.

E4.justification: Relative to v1 Figure 6, v2 Figure 4 adds a modality-gap visualization without homogeneous alignment and replaces the full-model plot, extending the visual comparison of the two alignment streams. The numerical component and strategy ablations, confusion matrices and sensitivity heatmaps are retained; much of Appendix C expands their interpretation.

E5.justification: v2 newly states that results are averaged over five runs and specifies seeds {1,2,3,4,5}; v1 provides neither disclosure. This does not establish an increase in runs. Neither version reports confidence intervals, standard deviations or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: DecAlign's previously tabulated benchmark and ablation scores remain unchanged. Baseline values change, including CGGM's MOSI Acc-2 from 84.43 to 82.73, and ReconBoost results are introduced. New CH-SIMS results include DecAlign Acc-3 of 88.24 and Corr of 0.657. AOBERT's MOSEI F1 changes from 83.14 to 83.64 in v2 Table 1, but v2 Table 6 retains 83.14.

T1.justification: The objectives, transport constraints and alignment mathematics in Equations 1–13 are unchanged. Appendices B.5–B.6 spell out standard formulas for the existing weighted metrics and moment estimates. These provide additional explanation and implementation detail, without a substantive theoretical revision or new proof.

C1.justification: Both versions claim modality decoupling, hierarchical prototype-transport and homogeneous alignment, and superior performance on four benchmarks. v2's explicit count of 13 comparison methods and its rewritten conclusion restate the existing contribution scope.

C2.justification: Appendix C adds extensive mechanism arguments distinguishing Hete's regression role, Homo's boundary smoothing, CT's margin preservation and greater sensitivity to transport/CT removal on MOSEI. Sections 3.2–3.4 also expand explanations of prototypes, skewness and transformer refinement. These go beyond v1's shorter effectiveness discussion, largely using retained evidence. The earlier conclusion's discussion of MLLM scaling and modality-collapse challenges disappears.

D1.justification: v2 supplies previously unavailable split counts, dataset-specific hyperparameters, feature extractors and dimensions, a 50-epoch training budget, and GMM fitting details. Its reproducibility statement also lists configurations, checkpoints, logs and scripts, while the abstract drops the direct repository URL and retains the project page. Some new specifications conflict: Table 4 lists BERT for IEMOCAP, whereas Appendix B.4 specifies DeBERTa.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations including ReconBoost, DLF, feature-extraction methods and medical/spatial application research, while dropping references such as Hwang et al.'s EMMA. These broaden the context, but the central positioning against global alignment and over-alignment remains intact. Much of Appendix A retains v1's related-work discussion.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the introduction and several method explanations, condenses main-text related work while retaining an extended appendix account, and replaces the future-work conclusion with a contribution summary. New ethics and reproducibility statements, appendix navigation and extensive interpretive prose substantially reorganize and expand the narrative.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to one and removes v1's introductory schematic. Benchmark tables are consolidated, detailed metrics redistributed to appendix tables, and the two ablation tables merged. Confusion matrices and radar plots are rearranged into horizontal panels; radar and modality-gap visualizations are combined. Dataset and hyperparameter tables are added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency by supplying the splits, feature pipelines, configurations and seed reporting that v1 left unspecified or referred to an absent appendix. Additional metrics and an ablation visualization provide limited further evidence. These benefits are tempered by conflicting IEMOCAP encoder specifications, inconsistent AOBERT scores between Tables 1 and 6, and Appendix C.4's near-co-location claim despite visibly separated modality clusters in Figure 4(h).
